ACIAR Monograph 143, published by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) in partnership with NSW Department of Primary Industries, the Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (CARDI), Murdoch University, University of Canberra, and MAFF, under ACIAR Project ASEM/2000/109. Uploaded PDF, 52 pages, image-only (Limon-font-era scan, read via page rasterization).
text:
This source mentions interplanting corn with Lemon basil (Ocimum basilicum citriodorum) as a low-cost practice that may help with pest management, based on the plant's strong aroma, which is described as having a repellent effect on mosquitoes and possibly some other insects. One suggested approach is planting a border row of Lemon basil around the edge of a corn field.

The source is candid that this companion-planting approach needs further evaluation and is presented as a low-cost practice worth trying rather than a proven, quantified pest-control method -- farmers interested in trying it should treat it as an experimental addition alongside, not a replacement for, the IPM practices described elsewhere in this source.
